title: RFdiffusion: designing new proteins with a diffusion model
summary: A guided diffusion model generates tailored protein structures, such as proteins that bind tightly to another molecule, and outperforms previous methods across a wide range of problems. The post says only that ‘a useful fraction’ of generated designs work as intended, without figures; the software was released in March 2023.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

evidence.tested: Designs were characterized experimentally (symmetric assemblies, metal-binding proteins, protein binders), and a cryo-EM structure of a designed binder was nearly identical to the design model; the abstract reports no overall success rates.
evidence.unknown: The abstract states no explicit limitations; the press post gives no success rates, sample sizes or benchmark numbers and says only that a useful fraction of designs work.
evidence.ai_role: A generative diffusion model fine-tuned from RoseTTAFold generated protein backbones for monomer, binder, oligomer, enzyme scaffold and motif designs.
